stage_a.note: Founders maintain a highly energetic and positive tone throughout their skit and presentation.
Founders show sustained engagement and excitement while explaining how the product works.
Founders introduce themselves with friendly smiles and an approachable demeanor.

venture.description: A natural garment and fabric cleanser spray designed to eliminate odors and kill bacteria on clothing.
venture.note: The founders act out a skit demonstrating the problem of germs on clothes before pitching.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder Pete introduces himself and his wife Bianca to the panel.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder Bianca states their ask of one hundred thousand dollars for ten percent equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete describes the germs a person encounters when leaving the house.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Bianca continues listing everyday activities that expose clothing to dirt and grime.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete notes that while people wash their hands, they do nothing for their clothes.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Bianca confirms that people currently do nothing to clean their clothes during the day.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete emphasizes that people cannot wear protective suits all day to stay clean.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Bianca points out the lack of products to clean clothes on the go.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete introduces the reason they created their product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete presents GarmaGuard as a natural garment and fabric cleanser to keep clothes fresh.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Bianca explains that applying the spray is an easy way to control dirt and grime.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete removes the protective suit from their model to show the product's effect.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Bianca states that the product is useful for everyone regardless of their profession.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete claims the spray gives people the freedom to live without wearing protective gear.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Bianca asks the panel who wants to partner with them.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete transitions to handing out samples and dismisses their model from the stage.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond jokes that he enjoyed their presentation, comparing it to a high school play.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Blake agrees with Daymond, calling the presentation fun and entertaining theater.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori tests the product by spraying the sample bottle she received.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Blake asks if the spray will remove smoke smell from clothes to avoid dry cleaning.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete confirms it works, noting they receive positive feedback from firefighters and police officers.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Blake remarks that the product works and asks if it is effective on shoes.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete briefly confirms that the product leaves no odor behind.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks about the mechanism the product uses to extract odors from fabric.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete explains that the spray eliminates the bacteria that cause the odors.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks for confirmation that the product actually kills the bacteria.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete confirms it kills germs and is lab tested, though not yet EPA registered.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks if the product is also effective at killing viruses.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete briefly confirms that it does kill viruses.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Blake specifically asks if the product can kill the COVID virus.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete admits they do not yet have the official claim for killing COVID.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Blake notes that obtaining that claim will significantly increase their sales.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Blake asks the founders to share their current sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete states they have been in business for over a year and shares their revenue.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond acknowledges that their sales figure is impressive and not a joke.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks if the founders have always worked in this type of business.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Bianca explains she is a nurse and worked until recently having a baby.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin congratulates the founders on the recent birth of their child.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Bianca explains the idea came from feeling dirty after her nursing shifts.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete adds that they needed a product to clean uniforms after watching her routine.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond asks about their current sales channels and how they plan to grow sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete answers that they currently sell on their own website and a few others.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks to confirm if their sales are exclusively online right now.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete briefly confirms that they only sell online.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks for the retail price and the manufacturing cost of the product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Bianca provides the selling price and the cost to produce each unit.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Blake compliments the founders on having a strong profit margin.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin reiterates that having a label claiming it kills COVID would be excellent marketing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete briefly asserts that they intend to get that specific claim.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Blake asks for the estimated timeline to secure the COVID kill claim.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete estimates it will take between six months and a year to get approval.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark exits, stating they need to be a great marketing company to compete effectively.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin exits, explaining he wants a product with an immediate COVID claim for marketing.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond exits, believing the business is strong enough to scale without an equity partner.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori exits, stating she likes the product but feels it is too early to invest.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Blake asks for their projected sales and profitability for the current year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pete provides their revenue target and expected profit margin for the year.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Blake exits, advising them to fund growth with cash flow rather than giving up equity.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori reflects on her own experience of bootstrapping a business without investors.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Blake agrees, noting that people often glorify investing when grinding is sometimes the better path.

decisions.note: Believes they need to be a great marketing company to compete and isn't ready to invest.
Wants a product with an explicit COVID kill claim and won't wait for the approval process.
Believes it is a good enough business that they do not need an equity partner to scale.
Likes the product and will be a customer, but feels it is too early for an investment.
Advises them to fund growth with cash flow and not give up equity before getting the COVID claim.

record.notes: The video contains several visible cuts during the questioning and decision phases. No offers were made by the investors.
